 Accelerating entry into the global market
Key participation that led to the success of Joseon beauty
Sales of TikTok shops and shops in the U.S 사진 확대 Swedish singer Zara Larsson showcases Depti's "Blue Peptide Eye Patch" on her TikTok account. [Picture = Goodbye to TikTok] Goodai Global, which has grown its body by acquiring K beauty brands such as Joseon Beauty and Tirtir one after another, will introduce its own beauty brand targeting the global market. The plan is to go beyond the strategy of acquiring and growing existing brands, plan and nurture brands directly, and speed up targeting global markets.
 On the 26th, Goodai Global announced that it will launch its first self-brand (PB) "Depti" aimed at the global market. Dept. will start selling around global online channels such as TikTok shops and Shopify in the U.S.
 The brand name Depti comes from the English word Depth, which means "deep." It contains a philosophy to look more deeply at products and consumers amid rapidly changing beauty trends.
 In particular, Dept. aims to become an indie brand that targets the niche market with experimental products rather than following the standardized success formula of the existing K-beauty brand. It is characterized by setting global consumers as major customers from the planning stage and designing product development and sales channels.
 The representative products are "Bonding Barrier Cream," which focuses on strengthening the skin barrier, and "Blue Peptide Eye Patch" for eye care.
 Among them, Blue Peptide iPatch was introduced by global pop star Zara Larson on her TikTok account and drew attention even before its launch. It is a dolphin-shaped product inspired by Jarrah Larson's signature makeup, and is gaining popularity around overseas online communities as fans share related content.
 Key personnel who led the global success of Korean beauty participated in Dept.'s brand development. Based on the experience of growing Korean beauty into a representative global K-beauty brand, it plans to establish a new brand in the overseas market.
 The brand launch is also noteworthy in that Goodai Global's business strategy is expanding.
 Goodai Global has been expanding its business by securing K-beauty brands with high growth potential such as Chosun Beauty, Tirtir, and RoundLab to combine global distribution networks and marketing capabilities.
 On the other hand, Dept. differs in that it directly promotes brand planning, product development, and global marketing. If it focused on raising the growth potential of existing brands, it is interpreted as a strategy to discover new demand through its own brands in the future.
 "If the existing method that has accelerated the growth of proven brands was the process of laying the foundation for growth, now it is time to create new growth potential with that capability," an official from Goodai Global said. "We will grow Dept. into a free indie brand that is not trapped in a standardized K-beauty formula."
 Meanwhile, Dept. is not Goodai Global's first in-house brand. Goodai Global previously introduced the Dermacosmetics brand 'Dr. 19'. However, if Dr. Nineteen is a Derma brand that focuses on skin care, Dept. is a brand developed to target global consumers from the planning stage. Its strategy is to target overseas niche markets by using local digital platforms in the U.S. as major sales channels and experimental products.
